canvas-01-1.description: The southern end of the Budd Lake settlement, on the east side of the lake south of the State Highway inset that crosses the sheet. The part runs from the State Highway (today US 46) and Brook along the lake shore south-east across a grid of summer-colony streets: Woodsedge Avenue, Foothill Avenue, Outlook Avenue, Kingden, Acton Place, Alton Place, Lakeview Avenue, Tulip Avenue, Prospect, Midland Avenue and the short arbitrary-numbered Avon, Barton and Brant Places at the east edge. The blocks are laid out in narrow lots and hold scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings, most of them named cottages (Home Nest, Gumpsewood, Wilkes Barre, Hazleton, Bonnie Brae Inn, Wildwood and many others), with private garages and a few auto sheds. There is no commerce or industry here apart from scattered outbuildings; the part is a seasonal residential subdivision. The State Highway runs along the west side next to the lake, whose shore and water are drawn at the left edge. Several streets are only partly built up and the lower right corner is mostly empty lots. The scale bar (100 ft to an inch) and the copyright line are printed at the bottom left. The part is drawn about six degrees out of line with the Spring Street blocks above the inset (part 2 of this sheet) and was placed separately for that reason.
notes: The State Highway is today US 46.
Lakeview Av. on this sheet is the continuation of Woodsedge Av. and is named Woodsedge Avenue in OpenStreetMap; today's Lakeview Avenue is another street on the north shore.
Kingden, Acton Pl., Alton Pl., Avon Pl., Barton Pl. and Brant Pl. have no street of that name in OpenStreetMap.
North arrow on the sheet is magnetic, about 10 degrees anticlockwise of true north.

Printed sheet 1 (canvas labelled Index). 100 ft to an inch. Three parts: part 1 Woodsedge, Foothill, Outlook, Tulip, Prospect, Midland Avs south of the lake's east shore; part 2 Spring St, High St, Center St and the Shore or Hackettstown Rd (Sand Shore Road) north of it, drawn at a rotation about 6 degrees different from part 1 (split at the State Highway inset); part 3 an inset strip of the State Highway (US 46) east of Netcong or Budd Lake Rd with Budd Lake School. Top right carries the key map (1000 ft to an inch), title, legend and specials index, excluded. North arrows are magnetic (about 10 degrees anticlockwise of true).

canvas-01-2.description: The east shore of Budd Lake north of the State Highway inset: the blocks between the Shore or Hackettstown Road along the water and the State Highway, from Spring Drive and Spring Street at the top of the sheet south to Cove. High and Center streets run parallel to the shore through long narrow blocks of summer cottages, each lot with a small frame dwelling and many with names (Love Nest, Happiness, Music Box, Harmony, Sunset Lodge, Glendale, Cheerio, Jack O Lantern, Sherwood Annex and others). Forest Drive and Spring Drive at the top left are laid out with lots but have few buildings; a note marks buildings there as being torn down. A tile-roofed dwelling stands by the Shore Road and a few cottages face the lake. The State Highway forms the east edge of the part, with house numbers along it and a couple of buildings on its far side. The part is purely residential and seasonal; no commerce or works are drawn. The lake shore with its water tint runs down the left side, and a large compass rose with a magnetic north arrow is printed near the top. This part continues on sheet 2 across Spring Street.
notes: The Shore or Hackettstown Rd. is today Sand Shore Road; the State Highway is US 46.
Spring Drive is today part of Spring Street; Forest Drive appears to be today's Hill Drive (not used for control).
High and Center are lettered without a suffix; today High Street and Center Street.
Split from part 1 because the two halves of the sheet fit about six degrees apart in rotation.
North arrow on the sheet is magnetic, about 10 degrees anticlockwise of true north.

canvas-01-3.description: A narrow inset across the middle of sheet 1, bounded by heavy lines, showing the State Highway north-east of the village where the Netcong or Budd Lake Road joins it. The highway runs the length of the strip with house numbers from about 401 to 440. In the gore between the two roads at the west end stand a store with gasoline tanks and other buildings; along the north side are scattered dwellings, a concrete auto repair garage and a second auto repair shop with gasoline tanks. On the south side are a concrete auto repairing garage, a township storage building and, at the east end, Budd Lake School, drawn 378 ft from the nearest building, with notes on its construction, heat and lighting. A note at the west end gives the distance to Elizabeth Lane on sheet 3. The strip has its own north arrow, pointing to magnetic north, and is drawn at a rotation very different from the rest of the sheet. The key numbers 25, 26 and 39 refer to blocks of the key map.
notes: The State Highway is today US 46 and the Netcong or Budd Lake Rd. is Netcong Road.

Placed from one hand-picked point (where the two roads' centrelines meet) with the atlas scale and a rotation of 44 degrees, the arrow's magnetic 34 degrees plus about 10 degrees declination; low confidence.
Budd Lake School (township school) stands at the east end of the strip.

sheet-2-1.description: The centre of Budd Lake village on the north-east shore of the lake: the blocks between the Shore or Hackettstown Road along the water and the State Highway, from Budd Avenue in the west to Spring Street and the State Highway in the south-east. Church, Grove, Orchard, Poole, Anderson Place, Gold Mine Road, Derby Place (a private road) and the Mt. Olive Road divide the area into blocks of cottages, many named (Swan Hill, Mountain View Inn, Bay Ridge, The Willows, Idlewild and others). Larger buildings include the Budd Lake Union Chapel by the Shore Road, the Hotel The Florence, the Budd House boarding house on the State Highway, Bluebeard Lodge, and the Grey Court Inn on the Mt. Olive Road east of the highway. On the lake shore are The Oasis, a club house, a dance hall and a toboggan slide. A stream crosses the lower part of the sheet into the lake. At the bottom right are the north ends of High and Center streets and Spring Street, which continue on sheet 1, and Spring Drive and Forest Drive, where buildings are marked to be torn down. A compass rose with a magnetic north arrow is printed at the left.
notes: The State Highway is today US 46; the Shore or Hackettstown Rd. is Sand Shore Road.
Poole is today New Street; Church, Grove and Orchard are Church Street, Grove Street and Orchard Street.
Mt. Olive Rd. west of the State Highway is today North Mount Olive Road, east of it Mount Olive Road.
Derby Pl. (private road) may be today's Baker Lane (not used for control).
Church St / Orchard St was rejected by the fit (9.8 m): the drawn junction does not match the modern one.

100 ft to an inch. Two parts: part 1 the main map between the lake and the State Highway (Church, Grove, Orchard, Poole, Anderson Pl, Gold Mine Rd, Mt. Olive Rd, Budd Av, Spring St, High, Center); part 2 above the heavy line, Sand Shore Rd along the north shore from Danby Pl to Hume Drive, drawn at another rotation.

sheet-2-2.description: A strip above the heavy line at the top of sheet 2 showing the Sand Shore Road along the north shore of Budd Lake, from beyond Danby Place in the west to Hume Drive in the east, where it continues on sheet 3. The strip is drawn at a different rotation from the rest of the sheet and lies some distance north-west of it on the ground. North of the road are summer cottages in small lots, almost all of them named (Colonial, Maple Lodge, Beau Sejour, Marigold, Margaret, Idle Wild, Wildwood, Idle Hour, Lazy Lodge, Inwood, La Casita, Luzern, Betty Jean, Cosy Corner, Palisade Cottage, West New York and others), along Danby Place, a paper street drawn dashed, Shady Lane and Canton Place. The house numbers along the road run from about 101 to 137. South of the road the strip is blank down to the heavy line. No commercial buildings are drawn; it is a seasonal cottage colony. A north arrow, pointing to magnetic north, is printed at the top right.
notes: Canton Pl. is today Lakeview Avenue (by position).
Danby Pl. is drawn as a dashed paper street; its position matches today's Knowles Lane but it was not used for control.
Hume Drive has no street of that name in OpenStreetMap; its corners with Sand Shore Rd were carried from sheet 3, which draws the same junction.

sheet-3-1.description: The north side of Budd Lake village: the blocks between the Shore or Hackettstown Road and Sand Shore Road along the lake and 4th Street and the State Highway, from 2nd Street and Hume Drive in the west to Budd Avenue in the east. The Netcong or Budd Lake Road runs straight up the western half, crossed by Waterloo Road, Hopkins, Cross, Dover Place and the numbered streets 1st to 4th; Stonewald Road and Dorset Place (a private road) run down to the shore. East of these, Elizabeth Lane, N. Rose Lane, S. Rose Lane, Rose Lane, William, Forest Road and Budd Avenue form long narrow blocks of summer cottages. Almost every lot holds a small frame dwelling, nearly all named (Mirasol, The House That Jack Built, Green Gander, Red Robin, Heather Bell, Sweet William, Blue Flower, Goldenglow, Woodbine, Geranium, Columbine and many more). The office of the Budd Lake News stands near Forest Road, and a few larger buildings stand off Dover Place. Along the State Highway at the top right are a few cottages in deep lots. The lake shore runs along the bottom, with the scale bar beneath it. The western strip around Hume Drive is marked as belonging to sheet 2.
notes: Renamed since: 4th St. east of Netcong Rd is Cornell Street, 3rd St. east of it Lafayette Street, the 2nd St. block east of Netcong Rd Yale Street, the 1st St. block east of it Betty Lane, and Dover Pl. Lehigh Street (by position); the 1st St. and 2nd St. west of Netcong Rd keep the names First Street and Second Street.
The Netcong or Budd Lake Rd. is today Netcong Road, the Shore or Hackettstown Rd. Sand Shore Road, and the State Highway US 46.
Abbot is today Abbott Street; Hopkins, William and Forest Lane are Hopkins Street, William Street and East Forest Road.
Today's Elizabeth Lane jogs at Rose Lane and loops into Forest Road near the shore; those junctions were left out.
Netcong Rd / Waterloo Rd was left out (6.9 m residual; Waterloo Road has been realigned).

100 ft to an inch. Two parts: part 1 the main map from Hume Drive and the 2nd/1st St blocks east to Budd Av, between the lake shore (Shore or Hackettstown Rd) and 4th St / the State Highway; part 2 a small inset at top right, the State Highway from Elizabeth La. to S. Rose La. further north-east.

sheet-3-2.description: A small inset in the top right corner of sheet 3, cut off by a heavy line, showing the State Highway further north-east, from Elizabeth Lane to South Rose Lane, beyond the edge of the main map. A note at Elizabeth Lane gives the distance of 235 ft to the detached strip of sheet 1. On the east side of the highway are deep lots with a few dwellings and a cement block manufacturing shed with gasoline tanks; the house numbers run from 351 to 358. The west side is laid out in lots with no buildings. The inset has its own north arrow, pointing to magnetic north, and carries the sheet title cartouche (Sept. 1929, Budd Lake, N.J.) and sheet number.
notes: The State Highway is today US 46.
Placed from one hand-picked point (Elizabeth Lane / US 46) with the atlas scale and a rotation of -58 degrees (the arrow's magnetic -68 degrees plus about 10 degrees declination); low confidence.
S. Rose La. here has no matching street name in OpenStreetMap.
